welcome.title: VideoDock Help
welcome.essentials: Before you start, check the four essentials: ① Cookie browser ② yt-dlp path ③ ffmpeg path ④ Download directory — all testable on the Settings tab.
welcome.intro: VideoDock is a graphical front-end for the open-source yt-dlp; it saves videos or audio from video sites to your disk.
welcome.features:
Features:
· Basic / Advanced modes; Advanced exposes any yt-dlp option with a live command preview
· Batch links, playlists, resume, proxy rotation
· Task queue and history, CSV export
welcome.sites: YouTube, Bilibili, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, SoundCloud and many more
welcome.sites_all: yt-dlp supports over a thousand sites; full list at:
toast.batch: All {n} tasks in this batch finished

inst.title: VideoDock Setup Wizard
inst.welcome_t: Welcome to the VideoDock Setup Wizard
inst.welcome_b: This wizard will unpack the bundled yt-dlp, prepare ffmpeg (downloading it if needed), auto-detect browser cookies, and write the configuration.
inst.mode_portable: Portable (recommended) — program and config live in one folder you can move anywhere
inst.mode_installed: Installed — program goes to the chosen folder, config to the system data directory
inst.ytdlp_b: yt-dlp is bundled with this setup; click Next to unpack it into the program folder.
inst.ffmpeg_missing: ffmpeg not found. It is required for merging and audio conversion; you must download it before continuing.
inst.cookie_b: Tests which browsers' cookies are usable (needed for logged-in downloads). The first working one is pre-selected; change it if you like.
inst.finish_b: Configuration written. VideoDock will start when you click Finish.
help.url: Media link. Video, audio or playlist pages; you can also drag links from the browser address bar into the box.
help.quality: Quality preset, translated into a -f selector: best = no limit; 1080/720/480 = that resolution or lower preferred.
help.audio_fmt: Transcode format in audio mode. Requires ffmpeg.
help.subs: Download subtitles, convert to srt and embed into the video file.
help.thumb: Embed the thumbnail into the media file metadata.
help.outdir: Save directory. Created automatically if missing.
help.o: -o, filename template. Fields: %(title)s title, %(id)s video ID, %(ext)s extension.
help.f: -f, format selector. e.g. bv*[height<=1080]+ba/b = best video up to 1080P merged with best audio.
help.merge: --merge-output-format, container after merging, usually mkv or mp4.
help.proxy: --proxy, download via a proxy such as socks5://127.0.0.1:1080. Empty = direct.
help.cookies: --cookies-from-browser, read cookies from a local browser for member/age-restricted content.
help.retries: --retries, automatic retries on network errors, default 10.
help.socket_timeout: --socket-timeout, seconds to wait for a response.
help.match_filter: --match-filter, filter entries, e.g. duration<600 keeps videos under 10 minutes.
help.download_archive: --download-archive, record downloaded IDs to skip duplicates; good for series.
help.no_playlist: --no-playlist, when a link points to both video and list, download only the video.
help.sub_langs: --sub-langs, subtitle languages. all = everything; or comma separated like zh-Hans,en.
help.embed_subs: --embed-subs, embed subtitles into the container (needs ffmpeg).
help.embed_metadata: --embed-metadata, write title/author metadata into the file.
help.recode: --recode-video, re-encode after download; slow, usually unnecessary.
help.no_part: --no-part, no .part temp file; resuming won't work if interrupted.
help.extra: Extra parameters: appended verbatim at the end; can override earlier options.
help.copy_cmd: Copy the full command to the clipboard so you can run it in PowerShell manually.
